blockers.issue: The `meeting` command is only isolated when it is the very first argv token. argparse accepts the top-level options (`--dry-run`, `--live`, `--config`, `--platform`, `--backend`, `--event`, `--doctor`) before the subcommand, and the post-parse dispatch chain in main_async has no `args.command == "meeting"` branch. A `meeting preview` invocation with any leading global option therefore falls through to `load_settings(args.config, **overrides)`, then MonitorStore/OSTagRunner/adapter construction, and in non-dry-run mode `adapter.start(runner)` — i.e. production config loading, business DB opening and a live adapter start from the 'isolated' synthetic command. The sitecustomize isolation test only exercises the `meeting`-first form, so this path is untested. Fix: after `build_parser().parse_args(argv)`, route `args.command == "meeting"` to run_preview_cli (or reject it) before any load_settings call.
blockers.reproduction: python -m ostag.main --dry-run meeting preview --input examples/meeting-preview.json --format json  → early dispatch is skipped (argv[0] is '--dry-run'), parse succeeds with command='meeting', no branch handles it, load_settings is invoked, then SystemExit('--event is required in dry-run mode'); no preview is printed. Same command with `--config <path>` and a non-dry-run config proceeds to create_adapter/adapter.start. Add the sitecustomize hook from test_early_dispatch_in_real_process_has_no_settings_db_or_network to the same invocation and it raises 'forbidden side effect' inside load_settings.

blockers.issue: safe_text (URL/domain stripping) is applied to already-validated typed identifiers (`tag`, `ref`, `environment`) when building facts. `tag` is restricted by regex to [A-Za-z0-9._-] and cannot contain a URL, yet the dotted-text heuristic replaces the whole tag with the omitted-link marker, so the release fact loses its typed identifier in the structured output. The shipped golden JSON evidence already shows this: the release_published fact has `"tag": "（链接已省略）"` instead of `v0.0.1-synthetic`. Branch refs with dots (e.g. `release/1.2`) are mangled the same way in facts and Markdown deployment/check lines. This contradicts the spec requirement to report necessary typed identifiers and not truncate facts; only the citation URL retains the real tag. Fix: for fields validated as safe identifiers, apply only HTML/Markdown escaping (or exempt validated tokens from URL_TEXT substitution).
blockers.reproduction: python -m ostag.main meeting preview --input examples/meeting-preview.json --format json | grep -n '"tag"'  → prints "tag": "（链接已省略）" for source gh-api-release (see FIXED VERIFIER EVIDENCE demo-json). Change the API PR/deployment `ref` to "release/1.2" in a copy of the fixture: facts and the Markdown lines render ref as `release/（链接已省略）` while matching still uses the raw value.

notes: Review based solely on the supplied files and fixed evidence; no tests were run and the candidate SHA256 was not recomputed.

Scope/grant simulation, half-open window on event_at (created_at/updated_at ignored), out-of-scope resource rejection before window filtering, single merge record per repo/PR, exact head check matching (repo+PR+ref+check_sha==head_sha), production deployment matching (repo+ref+merge_sha+environment=='production', in-window only), bare-#N ambiguity listing all candidate repos, explicit-reference-only Feishu linking, deployment_unverified phrased as unknown rather than false, coverage manifest exactness (missing/duplicate/extraneous rejected, failed/denied cannot carry records), needs_input=3 with partial output, and citation construction from frozen owner/repo plus typed IDs all appear correct in the code as written and are consistent with the demo output.

Bare-reference detector gap (not blocking, but the doc overstates it): the regex `(?<![\w])#([1-9][0-9]{0,18})\b` relies on \b and a \w lookbehind, and CJK characters are \w in Python's Unicode regex. Text like `看#12需要再确认` (no spaces, the common Chinese form) raises no ambiguity at all. Consider `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])#([1-9][0-9]{0,18})(?![0-9])` and document the literal rule precisely.

run_preview catches ValueError/TypeError/KeyError/OSError/RecursionError/OverflowError but not AttributeError. Whether a non-dict `request`/`mapping`/`grant`/`partitions[i]` payload can surface an AttributeError from the reused from_dict/_keys validators (yielding a traceback and exit 1 instead of the bounded exit-2 error) cannot be verified from the supplied materials; a test with `"request": "x"` and `"partitions": ["x"]` would close this.

The doc claims the window may not extend past the fixture observed_at, but this module does not check `window.end <= observed_at` itself; it relies on freeze_meeting_scope with `now=observed_at`. Unverified here; if freeze does not enforce it, the doc claim is inaccurate.

JSON `text`, `goal`, `reason`, and identifier fields contain Markdown backslash escapes and HTML entities (e.g. `\#12`, `'`), so `--format json` is a sanitized display projection rather than raw text. Acceptable given SourceRef.content_sha256 is over the original text, but consumers should be told the JSON strings are pre-escaped.
Citation URL for deployment_success uses `/deployments/<id>`, which is not a standard GitHub page; fine for a synthetic preview but should not be described as a real GitHub link format.
test_real_cli_json_markdown_and_installed_entrypoint asserts an `ostag` console script exists beside sys.executable; this couples the suite to the validation venv layout.
load_bundle uses os.O_NOFOLLOW/os.mkfifo (POSIX only); acceptable since cross-OS runs are explicitly out of scope, but note it for any future portability work.

Future live collection, authenticated grant issuance, authorization re-check, and human acceptance remain out of scope and are correctly documented as such; nothing in this candidate claims live or production acceptance.
